subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Epilepsy surgery, trigeminal neuralgia and DBS targets

steps.say: Epilepsy is called drug-resistant after two adequate anti-seizure trials are failing. Video-EEG with epilepsy-protocol MRI is then localising the focus. Surgery is beating a third drug once resistance is proven.
steps.tx: **Drug-resistant epilepsy** means 2 drug failures on appropriate antiepileptic schedules, and such patients go to comprehensive epilepsy surgery evaluation rather than endless drug rotations. Pseudo-resistance from nonadherence is excluded first. Early referral avoids years of uncontrolled fits. Resective surgery is offered when a single focus is found.

vis.alt: Brain illustration showing an epileptogenic focus with glutamate excitation, reduced GABA inhibition, thalamocortical spread and spike-wave discharge.
vis.caption: Focal hypersynchrony with thalamocortical spread defines the surgical target. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Febrile seizures in childhood are sometimes scarring the hippocampus for life. Refractory temporal lobe epilepsy is following with classic auras. Removing the front of the lobe is freeing most of these patients.
steps.tx: **Mesial temporal sclerosis** after febrile seizures causes refractory temporal lobe epilepsy, and anterior temporal lobectomy gives 60 to 70 percent seizure freedom versus continued medical therapy. Deja vu with rising epigastric aura marks the focus. Hippocampal volumetry quantifies the asymmetry.

steps.say: Dominant-side memory is tested before any temporal resection is planned. Selective removal may spare language and recall, but results are mixed. Neuropsychology is deciding which operation the patient can afford.
steps.tx: Selective **amygdalohippocampectomy** may spare language and memory compared with full lobectomy for dominant-hemisphere MTS, but the benefit is inconsistent, so the choice is individualised by neuropsychology and Wada or fMRI. Wada or fMRI maps reserve on both sides. Dominant disease favours the selective route when testing predicts cost. Patients are counselled with their own test scores.

steps.say: Discordant noninvasive data is sending depth electrodes into the brain. Drop attacks are injuring though never localising, so callosotomy is stopping the falls. Hemispherotomy is curing selected children with diseased halves.
steps.tx: **Stereo-EEG** with depth electrodes maps non-lesional networks, corpus callosotomy stops drop attacks in Lennox-Gastaut, and hemispherotomy cures Rasmussen and Sturge-Weber children. Each tool answers a different discordance. Hypotheses are framed before any electrode enters. Vagal stimulation palliates generalised and multifocal epilepsy without a resectable focus.

steps.say: Electric-shock face pain with trigger zones is starting with carbamazepine. A superior cerebellar loop is compressing the root entry zone on imaging. Procedures are waiting until drugs are failing.
steps.tx: Trigeminal neuralgia from superior cerebellar artery compression gives electric shock V2-V3 pain with trigger zones fired by touch, and **carbamazepine** is first-line before any procedure. Light touch triggers each volley. Carbamazepine doses are titrated to pain freedom. Attack diaries guide each dose change.

vis.alt: Trigeminal nerve divisions with neurovascular compression by superior cerebellar artery loop and first-line carbamazepine note, beside facial nerve course.
vis.caption: V2-V3 shock pain from superior cerebellar loop starts with carbamazepine. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Young healthy patients with confirmed contact are offered open decompression with padding. Balloon, glycerol or focused radiation is serving the elderly and multiple sclerosis cases. Fitness is deciding the invasiveness.
steps.tx: Microvascular **Jannetta decompression** with Teflon padding suits young healthy patients with MRI-confirmed contact, while balloon compression, glycerol or Gamma Knife suit the elderly and MS-related cases. Jannetta decompression separates vessel from nerve durably. Frailty steers toward percutaneous options. Recurrence prompts repeat imaging before reoperation.

steps.say: Levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease with wearing off is meeting stimulation after five years. STN and GPi targets are smoothing fluctuations while Vim is calming tremor. Medication is never stopped, only lightened.
steps.tx: Deep brain stimulation with STN stimulation or GPi stimulation smooths **motor fluctuations** in levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease after 5 years of therapy, and Vim stimulation controls essential tremor and dystonic tremor. Fluctuation diaries guide programming. Drugs continue at lower doses. Battery life is discussed at consent.

vis.alt: Man with postural and head tremor beside coronal brain showing DBS electrode in the Vim thalamus.
vis.caption: Vim thalamic DBS for tremor; STN or GPi targets smooth Parkinson fluctuations. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Generalised childhood dystonia including DYT1 is responding to pallidal stimulation. Diffuse spasticity is managed with spinal pumps while diplegic cerebral palsy is meeting selective rhizotomy. Strength is deciding candidacy.
steps.tx: GPi dystonia care means GPi stimulation treats generalised dystonia including DYT1 children, intrathecal baclofen pump manages diffuse spasticity, and selective **dorsal rhizotomy** suits spastic diplegic cerebral palsy with good strength. Strength predicts rhizotomy success. Pumps are refilled on schedule. Physiotherapy continues after every intervention.

vis.alt: Line drawings of cervical dystonia with torticollis, blepharospasm and writers cramp with abnormal posture.
vis.caption: Cervical, blepharospasm and task-specific dystonia phenotypes guide GPi targeting. Credit: StewardMD.
